mint-installation.title: Installation
mint-installation.summary: Install Linux Mint and discover an open-source operating system designed for simplicity and performance.

steps.text: Go to https://linuxmint.com/
Select your preferred Linux Mint edition
Select a mirror link to download the Mint ISO.
Open the Rufus website. Rufus is used to turn the ISO into a bootable USB installer.
Download the latest Rufus release.
Run Rufus after it finishes downloading..
Plug in your USB drive and select it under Device.
Choose the Mint ISO, start the process, and confirm ISO Image mode when Rufus asks.
steps.warning: This will delete the files on the USB drive. Back up important files before continuing.

steps.text: After Rufus finishes, keep the USB plugged in and restart the computer.
After device restart, choose "Start Linux Mint" to normally start the system.
Choose your preferred language along with your keyboard layout.
Toggle on "Install media codeds", this option is recommended to support various video formats to render in some websites.

Choose what type of installation you want to do. "Erase disk and install Linux Mint" will delete all files and programs inside your chosen drive. Choosing "Something else" will let you create or resize your own partitions.
steps.warning: This will delete the files on the USB drive. Back up important files before continuing.

steps.text: Select your timezone. This will set your system's internal clock.
Enter your account details and wait for the operating system to install.

mint-basic-navigation.title: Basic Navigation
mint-basic-navigation.summary: Master the fundamentals of the Linux Mint desktop by learning how to navigate the traditional layout and access the Terminal.

steps.text: Open the Terminal by searching "Terminal" in the Application Menu.
View which Directory you are currently in by typing "pwd".
List all files and folders in the current directory using "ls".
Change your current directory using "cd directoryName".
"cd .." allows you to go back to the previous directory.
Go back to your home director by typing "cd ~".

lessons.title: Creating and Managing Files and Folders

steps.text: Open the Terminal by searching "Terminal" in the Application Menu.
Create a new folder by typing "mkdir directoryName".
Create a new file: "touch fileName.txt" (You can also use other file types such as .html, .css, .js etc.).
Remove files by typing "rm fileName.txt".
Remove directories by typing "rmdir directoryName".
steps.warning: You cannot remove a directory if there are files inside it.

lessons.title: Moving and Renaming Files and Directories

steps.text: Open the Terminal by searching "Terminal" in the Application Menu.
The "cp fileName.txt" command (copy) is used to copy files and directories.
You can also specify the location of what directory the file will be copied by typing "cp fileName path/to/directory".
The "mv path/to/file" command (move) is used to move files and directories.
You can also use "mv oldName.txt newName.txt" to rename files.

mint-terminal-commands.title: Terminal Commands
mint-terminal-commands.summary: Master essential Linux Mint terminal commands to efficiently navigate files and execute administrative tasks.

steps.text: Open the Terminal by searching "Terminal" in the Application Menu.
The uname command displays system information: "uname -a" to display all system information, "uname -s" to show only the kernel name and "uname -r" to display the kernel release version.
Type "hostnamectl" and press Enter to view hostname and OS information.
Type "df -h" and press Enter to display disk space.
Open the Terminal by searching "Terminal" in the Application Menu.
The "ping siteName.com" command tests connectivity to a remote host.
"traceroute websiteName.com" shows the path packets take to reach a destination.
The "ifconfig" command displays network interface information.

The "ip" command is the modern replacement with more features. ip addr show to display IP addresses of all interfaces, ip route show to display the routing table and ip link show to display link layer information.
Type "top" and press Enter to display real-time system statistics (press q to quit)..

mint-app-installation.title: App Installation
mint-app-installation.summary: Discover how to safely install and manage software directly from the Terminal using Mint's powerful APT package and Snap manager.

lessons.title: Package Management Basics and APT Commands

steps.text: Linux Mint uses the APT (Advanced Package Tool) package manager to install, update, and remove software. APT manages software packages from repositories. A repository is a remote server that stores software packages.
Open the Terminal by searching "Terminal" in the Application Menu.
To find packages before installing them, use the "apt search" command.
To get detailed information about a package before installing it, use "apt show".
To install a package, use the "sudo apt install appName" command.
To view installed packages on your system, use "apt list" command.
Type "apt list --upgradable" and press Enter to see packages that can be upgraded.
To update installed packages to their latest versions, use "sudo apt upgrade".

mint-troubleshoot.title: Troubleshoot
mint-troubleshoot.summary: Equip yourself with the command-line tools and resolve package manager and software issues.

lessons.title: Managing Frozen Processes and Resource Exhaustion

steps.text: Open the Terminal by searching "Terminal" in the Application Menu.
Identify the Rogue Process in Real-Time, type "htop" to open process manager.
steps.warning: If htop is unavailable, type in "sudo apt install htop".

steps.text: If htop is too cluttered, search for the exact PID of the malfunctioning application by its name using "pgrep -l appName".
Terminate the unresponsive application by typing "kill appPID".
If the application is completely frozen and ignores the previous command, force it to close immediately using "kill -9 appPID".

fedora-installation.title: Installation
fedora-installation.summary: Essential steps to install Fedora Linux on your system, from downloading the ISO to completing your first boot.

steps.text: Go to "https://fedoraproject.org/"
Scroll down to see the Fedora Editions, Choose "Fedora KDE Plasma for Desktop" for a much user-friendly Fedora environment then click "Download Now"
In the Download page, click the download button for "Intel and AMD x86_64 systems" ISO file.
Open the Rufus website. Rufus is used to turn the ISO into a bootable USB installer.
Download the latest Rufus release.
Run Rufus after it finishes downloading..
Plug in your USB drive and select it under Device.
Choose the Fedora ISO, start the process, and confirm ISO Image mode when Rufus asks.
steps.warning: This will delete the files on the USB drive. Back up important files before continuing.

steps.text: After Rufus finishes, keep the USB plugged in and restart the computer.
After system restart, choose whether to install Fedora in your hard drive or keep exploring it's environment without installing.
Choose the Fedora ISO, start the process, and confirm ISO Image mode when Rufus asks.
steps.warning: This will delete the files on the USB drive. Back up important files before continuing.

steps.text: After Rufus finishes, keep the USB plugged in and restart the computer.

fedora-basic-navigation.title: Basic Navigation
fedora-basic-navigation.summary: Learn the essential Fedora Linux terminal commands for navigating directories, managing files, and exploring the system.

steps.text: Open Terminal/Konsole by searching in applications menu.
The "pwd" command displays your current directory location.
"ls" command displays files and folders in your current directory.
To change your directory, type "cd directoryName".
Type "cd .." to go back to the previous directory.
Go back to your home directory using "cd ~".

fedora-terminal-commands.title: Terminal Commands
fedora-terminal-commands.summary: Master essential Fedora terminal commands to efficiently control files, directories, and system operations.

steps.text: Open Terminal/Konsole by searching in applications menu.
Search for files and directories using "find ~ -name "fileName.txt"".
Locate a Command using "which commandName".
Open a Manual Page using "man ls".
The terminal displays available options and explanations for the "l --help" command.

fedora-app-installation.title: App Installation
fedora-app-installation.summary: Learn how to install, manage, and remove applications in Fedora Linux using essential tools like DNF, Flatpak, and RPM

lessons.title: Installing Applications Using DNF (Fedora Package Manager).

steps.text: Open Terminal/Konsole by searching in applications menu.
Before installing, search for a package by typing "dnf search appName".
To install the package, type in "sudo dnf install appName -y".
steps.warning: sudo gives admin permission, -y automatically confirms installation

steps.text: Uninstall the package by typing "sudo dnf remove appName -y".

fedora-troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
fedora-troubleshooting.summary: Identify, diagnose, and resolve common Fedora Linux issues using essential troubleshooting commands and system tools

steps.text: Open Terminal/Konsole by searching in applications menu.
Check System Uptime and Load using "uptime".
To check memory usage, type "free -h".
You can also check available system disk space, type "df -h".
To view if there are critical system errors, use "journalctl -p 3 -xb".
